title: U.S. Manufacturing Is Adding Jobs Again, but the Hiring Rules Have Changed - WSJ
content:
The U.S. is adding manufacturing jobs again. The catch: You might need a college degree to get one.

That shift has big ramifications for the U.S. economy. Higher-skill jobs tend to pay better and create greater profits for their employers, boosting growth. But because these roles require more education, companies risk a skilled-worker shortage if training programs don’t keep pace.
